extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, chymists, and learned readers interested in experimental philosophy (17th-century/early chemistry)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging experimental and theoretical claims about the composition and properties of bodies in early chemical/natural-philosophical inquiry; emphasizes what counts as adequate proof, explanation, and experimental practice. Useful for assessing claims that bodies are composed of particular 'elements' or 'principles'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental evidence must demonstratively support conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiments wont to be brought, whether by the common Peripateticks, or by the vulgar Chymists, to demonstrate that all mixt bodies are made up precisely either of the four Elements, or the three Hypostatical Principles, do not evince what they are alledged to prove.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept experiments that only superficially or precariously support a theoretical conclusion. Scrutinize whether the experimental observations actually entail the claimed elemental composition rather than relying on suggestive or ambiguous results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false dichotomy in hypothesis evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: many questions... may admit of so many Differing Hypotheses, that 'twill be very inconsiderate and fallacious to conclude (except where the Opinions are precisely Contradictory) the Truth of one from the falsity of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple plausible hypotheses exist, the failure of one does not automatically validate another. Consider and test alternative explanations rather than inferring truth by elimination unless hypotheses are strictly contradictory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanations must address causes and mechanisms, not only subjects of qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: it is one thing to know the subject wherein a Quality principally resides, and another thing to have a right notion and knowledge of the quality itself... How little do I know more then any Ordinary Man of Gravity, if I know but that the Heaviness of mixt bodies proceeds from that of the Earth they are compos'd of, if I know not the reason why the Earth is Heavy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A satisfactory account should explain why a quality arises (mechanism), not merely identify the material 'seat' or component in which the quality is found. Seek causal explanations beyond nominal assignment to an element or principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties often depend on motion, texture, and arrangement of parts
rubrics_metrics.description: the greatest part of the affections of matter, and consequently of the Phænomena of nature, seems to depend upon the motion and the continuance [contrivance] of the small parts of Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider microscopic structure, arrangement, and motion of parts (texture) as causes of observable properties (e.g., colour, hardness) rather than attributing them solely to the presence or proportion of material ingredients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separated products from heat or solvents are not necessarily pure elementary bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: in chymical resolutions the separated Substances were pure and simple Bodies; no one would be indued with more Specifick Vertues, than another; and their qualities would Differ as Little as do those of Water. ... the separated Substances... are yet each of them compounded of the four Elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat substances obtained by fire, distillation, or solvent extraction as potentially composite or newly recombined materials; do not assume that an operation yields pure 'elements' simply because it separates observable fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious using sensory/taste evidence (e.g., saltness) as proof
rubrics_metrics.description: the Saline part of Ashes is very strongly Tast[ed], and easily soluble in Water; ... I could not perceive that the force of the Fire had imparted to it the least Saltness, or so much as made it less Insipid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensory impressions (taste, smell, colour) can be misleading or altered by processing; corroborate sensory claims with other observations and controls before inferring composition or elemental presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish apparent (optical) phenomena from real/permanent properties
rubrics_metrics.description: it may be objected, that these are not real, but apparent Colours; that I may not lose time in examing the Distinction, I will alledge against the Chymists, a couple of examples of Real and Permanent Colours...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether observed phenomena (e.g., colours produced by prisms or heating) are merely transient/optical or truly intrinsic and permanent; permanence and reversibility are diagnostic tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solvent extracts commonly yield compounded, finer corpuscle mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: That Water will dissolve not only pure Salts, but Crystals of Tartar, Gumme Arabick, Myrr'h, and Other Compound Bodies. As also Spirit of Wine will Dissolve not only the pure Sulphur of Concretes, but likewise the whole Substance of divers Resinous Bodies...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging what a solvent 'extracts', assume extracts may be complex mixtures of finer parts rather than pure elementary substances; further separations (e.g., distillation) may reveal additional components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental method and management change outcomes—do not generalize across methods
rubrics_metrics.description: sometimes this or that Body affording a greater number of Differing substances by one way of management, than the same yields by another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that technique, temperature, apparatus, and procedure influence what substances are recovered; avoid universal claims about composition based on a single mode of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purification may reduce practical efficacy—balance theoretical purity and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: though such compleatly purifyed Ingredients of Bodies might perhaps be more satisfactory to our Understanding; yet others are often more useful to our Lives, the efficacy of such Chymical Productions depending most upon what they retain of the Bodies whence they are separated, or gain by the new associations...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating preparative methods, consider both epistemic clarity and practical effects: excessively pure isolates may lose valuable properties; usefulness can derive from retained or newly acquired textures/associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism is warranted where competent proof is absent
rubrics_metrics.description: this seems to me a sufficient reason to doubt of a known and important proposition, that the Truth of it is not yet by any competent proof made to appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt doubt for propositions lacking competent proof; require adequate, relevant, and replicable evidence before accepting foundational claims (e.g., existence/number of elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not infer elemental necessity from observed generation/transmutation phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Water may be Transmuted into all the other Elements; from whence it may be inferr'd, both, That 'tis not every Thing Chymists will call Salt, Sulphur, or Spirit, that needs alwayes be a Primordiate and Ingenerable body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider natural processes (growth, transmutation) that produce complex bodies from simpler ones; such phenomena undermine claims that particular elements must be present a priori to form certain concretes.
